programme.title: The Darwinian Revolution
programme.sub-title: The Way It Used to Be
programme.desc: Examining the traditional worldview in the West, which is based on the biblical account of creation fixed at 4004 B.C.; an allied idea is the Great Chain of Being, pictured as an immutable scale of life forms from the most primitive to God himself.

programme.title: The Darwinian Revolution
programme.sub-title: Theories of Evolution in the 18th Century
programme.desc: Studying three 18th-century thinkers; Benoit de Maillet, who estimates the age of the cosmos; Georges Buffon, who believes living things descend from more primal forms; Pierre Simon Laplace, who proposes a theory for the solar system's formation.

programme.title: The Darwinian Revolution
programme.desc: At the end of the 18th century, fossils are not necessarily regarded as actual remains of living things; they become central to the work of Georges Cuvier, who connects them to extinct species which he believes died out in violent catastrophes.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Cosmology takes the entire universe as its subject, not just its form, structure and contents, but also the manner of its birth and evolution; looking at the origin of cosmology in creation stories and its relation to the journey ahead.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Introducing the hierarchy of structures in the universe; from planets to stars, galaxies, galaxy clusters and larger groupings of galaxies called the cosmic web; light travels at a finite speed, looking far away also means looking far back in time.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: Discussing cosmic properties; the universe is lumpy at the scale of galaxies and galaxy clusters; at larger scales, it is smooth and similar in all directions; this property of homogeneity and isotropy is called the cosmological principle.

programme.title: Cosmology: The History and Nature of Our Universe
programme.desc: The most familiar constituents of the universe are atomic matter and light; neutrinos make up another component; 96 percent of the universe is dark energy and dark matter; the relative amounts of these constituents changes as the universe expands.

programme.title: Unlocking the Hidden History of DNA
programme.desc: Investigating the independent discoveries of genes and of DNA in the mid-1800s; following both trails into the 20th century, as chromosomes are discovered and the realization finally begins to dawn that genes and DNA may be related.

programme.title: Unlocking the Hidden History of DNA
programme.desc: Joining the quest to understand the molecular biology of the gene with the famous blender experiment, which shows that DNA, not proteins, transmits genetic information; looking at five scientists who compete to solve the mystery of DNA's structure.

programme.title: Unlocking the Hidden History of DNA

programme.title: Unlocking the Hidden History of DNA
